statement: Organizers of a charity fun run lower the registration fee as more runners sign up. If $n$ runners register, each runner pays $50 - 0.1n$ dollars, for $n$ up to $400$. What is the least number of runners for which the total registration money is at least $\$5{,}760$?

choices.misconception: I ignored the discount and used $\$50$ per runner, so $5760 \div 50 = 115.2$, which I rounded up to 116.
I found the number of runners that brings in the most money, $n = 250$, instead of the least number that reaches $\$5{,}760$.
I solved $n(50 - 0.1n) = 5760$ correctly but chose the larger solution, 320.

hints: Total money is the number of runners times the fee each one pays.
Solve $n(50 - 0.1n) = 5760$. Multiplying both sides by $-10$ gives $n^2 - 500n + 57600 = 0$.
The quadratic formula gives $n = \tfrac{500 \pm \sqrt{250000 - 230400}}{2} = \tfrac{500 \pm 140}{2}$. The money is at least $\$5{,}760$ between the two roots.

solutions.reliable: Total money is $R = n(50 - 0.1n)$. Setting $R = 5760$ gives $50n - 0.1n^2 = 5760$, so $n^2 - 500n + 57600 = 0$ and $(n - 180)(n - 320) = 0$. The graph of $R$ is a parabola opening downward, so $R \ge 5760$ for $180 \le n \le 320$. The least number of runners is $180$. Check: $180 \times (50 - 18) = 180 \times 32 = 5760$, while $179$ runners bring in $179 \times 32.1 = 5745.9$ dollars, which is short.
